paragraphs: What is up, developers? Welcome back to GitHub Awesome Episode 31 of GitHub Trending Weekly. 35 repositories trending on GitHub right now. Let's get into it.

Microsoft released Trellis 3D 2.0, a state-of-the-art image-to-3D model. The catch: it was locked to Nvidia GPUs because it relied on custom CUDA kernels. Trellis Mac ports the entire 4-billion-parameter model to run natively on Apple Silicon via PyTorch MPS. The developer rewrote the CUDA-specific sparse 3D convolutions and mesh extraction algorithms into pure Python and PyTorch.

OpenMythos is an open-source PyTorch reconstruction of what the research community believes Claude Mythos is: a recurrent depth transformer. Instead of stacking hundreds of layers, it uses a looped recurrent block with sparse mixture-of-experts routing. Instead of chain-of-thought where the model physically prints intermediate tokens, OpenMythos performs multi-step reasoning entirely inside continuous latent space.

Zennotes is a keyboard-first desktop notes app. Plain, portable Markdown files on disk, full Vim modal editing, live rendering for math plots and architecture diagrams from fenced code blocks. Wire it directly into Claude Desktop, Cursor, or Claude Code. Your AI seamlessly reads your project plans, searches your knowledge base, and writes research directly into your actual Markdown files on disk.

PGQue is a zero-bloat PostgreSQL message queue implemented in pure PL/pgSQL. No C extensions, no external daemons, one SQL file dropped into your database plus pg_cron to keep it ticking. Instead of heavy per-row deletions, it uses snapshot-based batching and truncate-based table rotation. Batch completes, entire active table gets truncated, expensive vacuum overhead completely bypassed.

CC Design is a structured design workflow skill that turns your local coding agent into an expert product designer. Enforces context-first design: before writing a single div, the agent actively hunts down your existing brand systems, UI libraries, and product code to guarantee new designs match your actual product. Playwright MCP visually verifies everything locally.

Most browser automation breaks the moment a site changes its DOM structure or throws an unexpected popup. Browser Harness connects directly to Chrome over WebSocket via Chrome DevTools Protocol. When the agent hits something unexpected, it injects its own JavaScript on the fly to handle it. No pre-written scrapers, no rigid rules. Plug it into Claude Code and watch it drive your browser.

AI agents aren't just stuck in terminals anymore; they're physically hacking hardware. AutoProber is an open-source flying probe stack that lets an AI agent control a cheap $220 desktop CNC machine. Place a raw circuit board on the bed, tell the agent there's a new target. The AI drives a USB microscope around, stitches a high-resolution map, uses vision to read IC labels, and autonomously identifies interesting test pads.

Lingbot-map is a 3D foundation model operating on a pure see-as-you-go principle. Standard single RGB camera, continuous camera pose estimation, dense 3D geometry reconstructed frame by frame in real time at around 20 frames per second. Powered by a feed-forward geometric context transformer. Borrows paged KV cache technology from LLMs to maintain trajectory memory across sequences longer than 10,000 frames without running out of RAM.

Frame-accurate video control in the browser has always been painful. The HTML5 video tag lags, drops frames, and scrubs imprecisely. ActiveFrame from creative agency Active Theory throws the video element out entirely. A custom AAF video format built for the modern WebCodecs API takes your video, extracts raw H.264 or H.265 samples, packs them with a JSON manifest into one lightweight binary.

Tired of Adobe Acrobat begging for a subscription? KillerPDF is a standalone Windows executable under 10 megabytes. No installer, no account, no subscription, zero telemetry. Drop it on a USB drive and it runs. PDF rendering, merge and split documents, drag-and-drop pages, reusable signatures, highlight overlays. Double-click any text to edit it inline and it automatically matches the original document's font.

Diagram Design is a Claude Code skill built by someone tired of fighting Figma for 30 minutes every time she needed an architecture sketch. Your agent becomes a high-end editorial graphic designer generating stunning self-contained HTML and SVG files. Zero JavaScript, zero external images, zero build steps, 13 built-in structural types including sequence diagrams, state machines, Venn diagrams, and swimlanes.

Using Enro means signing up, dealing with session limits, and getting pushed toward paid tiers. HostC is a blazing-fast, zero-config edge tunneling tool built entirely on Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects. One CLI command instantly exposes your localhost with a secure HTTPS URL, native WebSocket proxying out of the box, something heavily restricted on most free tunneling services.

Design.md files fix AI hallucinating ugly generic UI, but manually writing design rules or extracting hex codes from sites you like takes forever. Design MD Chrome automates it. Navigate to any beautiful website, click the extension, and it instantly rips the entire design language directly from the live DOM: typography scales, spacing variables, brand colors, shadow effects, using Cursor in your IDE, Claude Code in...

...your terminal, Windsurf for second opinions. Each one has isolated memory. Teach one a rule, the others forget it. Agentic Stack fixes that. One brain, many harnesses. A portable agent folder that standardizes your AI's memory, custom skills, and protocols. Drop it into your project and it plugs into Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, OpenClaw, or even a custom Python loop.

Government spending data lives in massive unreadable spreadsheets. Nemesis is an open-source AI auditing dashboard that ingests millions of rows of public procurement data and uses LLMs to instantly flag anomalies, markup, and wasted taxpayer money: luxury SUVs, absurdly priced billiard tables, all the stuff hidden in regional budgets. Turns unreadable spreadsheets into a clean, searchable database with color-coded risk flags.

Googling for PDF to Word or JSON formatter always lands you on shady ad-filled sites trying to steal your data. Your Everyday Tools bundles 57 utilities into one self-hosted dashboard. Text, calculator, and security tools run entirely client-side in vanilla JS. Document conversions use purely in-memory processing on the server, so your sensitive files are never written to disk.

Open Carousel is an open-source AI-powered Instagram carousel builder running entirely local. Type 'start' in Claude Code. Teach it your brand colors, fonts, and logo once, then just tell it what to post: 'Make me a five-slide post about learning React,' and your agent autonomously designs the entire carousel slide by slide. Preview live in your browser, ask Claude to tweak layouts in chat, export perfectly sized PNGs for Instagram.

Native iOS and Android apps have satisfying UI clicks and pops. Web apps have been silent for 30 years because shipping MP3s is slow and bloated. Tiks fixes that in 2 KB. Zero audio files. It generates crisp clicks, toggles, success chimes, and error buzzes dynamically at runtime using pure Web Audio API synthesis and oscillators. Design custom sound themes by tweaking frequency, oscillator type, and decay.

Stop uploading your images, videos, and PDFs to slow ad-filled compression sites. Dinky is a small macOS utility, just 14 megabytes. Drag and drop, paste from clipboard, or set it to auto-watch a folder. Instantly converts heavy images into WebP. It automatically detects whether an image is a photograph or a screenshot and dynamically adjusts compression quality for the perfect balance of file size and visual clarity.

GridEx is a native database IDE built specifically for macOS in Swift and AppKit with a Windows version in WinUI 3. Connects to PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, and Redis from one keyboard-driven interface. Built-in AI assistant that actually understands your database schema. Connect to Claude, OpenAI. Type plain English, get perfect SQL queries executed automatically.

MDV is a Markdown superset built for documents, dashboards, and slides. Extends standard Markdown so you can embed data and visualizations directly in your text. Fenced code blocks render instantly into gorgeous SVG charts and KPI stats. Layout containers let you build complex grids without writing any messy HTML. Everything exports to a single self-contained HTML or PDF.

USB Uncensored LLM is a zero-install plug-and-play local AI environment. Run high-quality models like Gemma and Nemotron directly from any USB drive or portable SSD. Fully air-gapped, zero internet required, zero dependencies left on the host machine. Plug it in and it natively executes on Windows, macOS, Linux, and even Android via Termux.

iMazing is the go-to iOS device manager until you look at the subscription price. Phosphor does the same job for free. Browse iOS backups without restoring. Export iMessage conversations to HTML or CSV. Extract camera roll photos. Install IPAs. Stream the device syslog in real time. Parses Apple's manifest database directly for file-system-style backup browsing without touching the backup itself.

Pasting web content into an AI agent means dumping navigation bars, ads, and hidden HTML tags into your context window alongside the actual content. MD This Page is a browser extension powered by Mozilla's Readability that converts any web page to clean Markdown with Alt+M or a right-click. Opens a preview tab where you can tweak formatting, toggle images, and copy directly into Claude or ChatGPT.

Cydintosh runs a real 68K Mac emulator on a $10 ESP32 display, complete with touchpad mouse control on the LCD. The clever part is the IPC bridge: custom homebrew Mac apps running inside the emulator communicate with the ESP32 chip underneath, so your emulated 1984 Macintosh can scan for Wi-Fi and pull live MQTT weather data from a modern Home Assistant setup.

Token Juice hooks into your terminal and compresses noisy command output before the LLM sees it: progress bars, verbose install logs, repetitive status messages squashed down to the dense signal your agent actually needs to keep working. Native Claude Code hook installer included. Less junk in the context window, lower API bill at the end of the month.

Adding smooth animations to terminal UIs in Rust usually means writing a lot of timing and interpolation logic from scratch. Animate is a zero-dependency animation crate with a macro-driven API that handles the boilerplate, built-in easing functions, custom interpolators, and playback modes including once, cycle, and alternate. Native Ratatui support behind a feature flag.

Vibe-coding a full application in a weekend and then having no idea how it actually works is a very specific and relatable problem. Claude Map installs into Claude Code, sends your repository structure to an architecture sub-agent, and renders an interactive conceptual map in your browser. Not a file tree, a map grouped by what the code actually does.

Ghosty's rendering performance is hard to beat, but the window management leaves some things to be desired. MacTerm wraps libghosty in a native Swift UI interface: vertical project sidebar, infinite split panes, a global dropdown terminal you can summon from anywhere. Workspace auto-persistence saves your entire pane layout and restores it exactly on next open.

AI agents hitting Cloudflare blocks and CAPTCHAs mid-task is one of those pipeline failures that's hard to debug and annoying to work around. Super Spider handles anti-bot bypass, headless browser rendering, and multi-engine search out of the box. The LLM-focused design is the practical difference: instead of dumping raw HTML into your context window, it converts pages directly to clean Markdown or structured JSON.

Neofetch shows your system specs. Fetch shows them while your distro logo spins in 3D. Single optimized C file, zero heavy dependencies, reads directly from /proc and sys. Takes your Linux distro's ASCII logo and extrudes it into a rotating 3D relief map with Blinn-Phong shading, specular highlights, and a Z-buffer. System stats tick and update in real time while it spins. Over 500 distro logos supported with original ANSI colors preserved.

Boxer3D turns a LiDAR-equipped iPhone into a real-time 3D object detector. A lightweight YOLO model handles 2D detection, then Boxer3D from Meta Research lifts those flat detections into fully oriented seven-degree-of-freedom 3D bounding boxes using LiDAR depth data and DINOv3 visual features. ARKit handles gravity and camera tracking. SceneKit anchors the 3D wireframes into your physical environment.

Most agent memory systems require a vector database, an embedding model, and a chunking strategy before you can store a single fact. Memkraft stores everything in plain human-readable Markdown. No vector embeddings, no infrastructure, zero dependencies. It autonomously extracts facts, classifies information, and maintains a compounding knowledge base that your agent reads and updates as local text files.

Building UIs in PowerShell means WPF, XAML, and frozen windows the moment a long script runs. PSUI fixes that with simple PowerShell functions and async background execution. The clever part is the custom PSHost that intercepts standard cmdlets: Write-Host pipes to a UI console panel with color support, Write-Progress drives a real graphical progress bar, Get-Credential pops a native credential dialog.

Aube is a Node.js/JS package manager written in Rust, up to 7x faster than pnpm and 3x faster than Bun in warm CI environments with a global content-addressable store that cuts disk usage significantly. It natively reads and writes your existing package-lock.json or bun.lock files in place. Use it locally for the speed boost while the rest of your team stays on whatever they're using.
